`just minds-stop` no longer kills the intentionally-detached latchkey daemon: subtrees rooted at a process that started its own session (the `mngr latchkey forward` supervisor and its `latchkey gateway` / `mngr observe --discovery-only` children, which are designed to outlive the desktop client so agent tunnels survive restarts) are now excluded from the wait-and-force-kill descendant walk. Zombie processes are no longer counted as alive (they cannot be killed and previously guaranteed a bogus force-kill report), and the SIGTERM grace is widened from 10s to 15s.

The `minds-dev-workflow` skill's "Clean shutdown" section is rewritten to describe the current cheroot-based backend (the old text described the pre-SPA uvicorn/`stream_manager` chain) and to document that the detached latchkey supervisor trio surviving a shutdown is correct behavior, not orphaned processes.
